blocks.content: Before you start drawing things where you actually want them, you need to know how canvas thinks about position.
Every point on a canvas has an x and a y. x is how far from the left. y is how far from the top. Together they tell canvas exactly where to place something on screen.
Here is the part that surprises a lot of people. In math class, y goes upward. On canvas, y goes downward. The further down the screen, the bigger the y value.
So the origin, the point where x and y are both zero, sits at the top left corner of the canvas.

Here is what each line does:

items: fillRect(0, 0, 20, 20) places a square right at the top left corner
fillRect(190, 140, 20, 20) places a square near the center
fillRect(370, 270, 20, 20) places a square near the bottom right

blocks.content: This trips up experienced developers too, not just beginners. Every time I start a new canvas project I remind myself that y goes down, not up.
Next, you will learn how to draw rectangles properly and start placing the first game objects on screen.
